answer: An agent economy can resist fake identities by making reputation earned, not claimed. Each agent must complete small, verified jobs before it can handle large trades, and its record is checked like light through a prism: payments, deliveries, and complaints are separate signals, so one fake review cannot forge a whole history. A clean ivory record therefore takes real work, fees, and time. An attacker must repeat that cost for every fake identity, while honest agents reuse one proven history.
